newsitem.title: USA: Brother of accused CIA shooter wants to come to US.
newsitem.headline: Brother of accused CIA shooter wants to come to US.

text.p: The oldest brother of Mir Aimal Kansi wants to come to the United States from Pakistan to help defend him against charges resulting from a 1993 shooting at CIA headquarters, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper quoted a Pakistani government source as saying that Hamidullah Kansi, 43, was "trying to come, but we are not sure what is the status of his efforts."
Richard Goemann, the public defender appointed to defend Mir Aimal Kansi, told the paper he had been in touch with the elder Kansi and hoped he would "assist us with this case."
A Virginia judge has set a Nov. 3 trial date for the younger Kansi after rejecting a defence request for even more time to prepare for the trial.
Kansi, 33, was apprehended in Pakistan and brought back to the United States last month to face murder and other criminal charges that carry the death penalty.

He has been charged with killing two people and wounding three others in the Jan. 25, 1993, morning rush hour shooting outside Central Intelligence Agency headquarters at Langley, Virginia, just outside Washington.
All but one of the victims were CIA employees.
